description: Declared cross-oracle key-set divergences. A row here is an HONEST DECLARED EXCEPTION, not a mute: it records a divergence that is real, understood, and owned by a named work-item. Rows are checked - one that no longer matches a live divergence is STALE and fails the audit, so this file cannot rot into a blanket mute. Text, diffable, in the proof lineage (no-binary-in-proof-lineage).

divergences.reason: Introduced by PR #10722 (work-item 081M00TYT8N087G0R003MPMRX9): TypeScript's TemperatureReadout gained a required `fidelity: ChannelFidelity` so that a dead sensor stops rendering as a calm room. F#'s TemperatureReadout (src/Core/Heat.fs) kept eight fields and both still declare v1. NOT resolved here, because the correct resolution is a design call about what `fidelity` MEANS and this audit's author does not own that. The asymmetry a resolver needs: ChannelFidelity is `exact | saturated | below-resolution | out-of-domain`, and the `out-of-domain` case is motivated by JavaScript `number` admitting NaN/Infinity, which F#'s `int`-typed TemperatureReadout.ofPpm CANNOT produce - so that case is genuinely TS-specific. But `saturated` (input above MaxPpm) and negative input are real on BOTH sides and F#'s `max 0 |> min MaxPpm` clamp discards them just as silently as TypeScript's did before the fix. So `fidelity` is not purely encoder-local, and the three live options (add to F# and keep v1 / bump to v2 / declare it a diagnostic excluded at the serialisation boundary) are all still open. One position this audit does hold: adding a REQUIRED field to an already-published v1 is a breaking change by the ordinary schema-evolution rule, so `keep v1 unchanged` is the weakest of the three.
